subject: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 29, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval
Attachments: hosted-api-throttling-messaging-draft-v3.md; 429-error-payload-examples.json

Wei/Elliot — can you do a final pass on the hosted API customer-facing messaging for the new throttling semantics?

Primary goals:
- Make the 429 meaning unambiguous (rate limit vs capacity protection) without exposing internal routing details.
- Provide actionable retry guidance (Retry-After + backoff + jitter) and prevent retry storms.
- Keep enterprise expectations aligned with Dedicated/contract language (no “guaranteed capacity” implication for Hosted).

We’re targeting to merge docs by EOW for the staged rollout.

Key questions:
1) Do we want “Over capacity” wording in addition to “Too Many Requests”? (My inclination: yes, in the docs + error reason code.)
2) Are the example payloads compatible with the SDK’s existing error parsing? (Elliot: call out if anything will break.)

If you’re good with it, reply with “approved” or inline edits.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Product — Hosted API
Redwood Inference



From: Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 29, 2025 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval

I did a pass. Overall direction is good. Proposed edits below (mostly tightening language + removing anything that reads like a promise).

A) Header terminology:
- In the docs, lead with “HTTP 429 (Throttled)” and then break down two causes:
  - rate_limit_exceeded
  - over_capacity
  Keeps the API stable but gives customers a handle.

B) Retry guidance:
- Recommend exponential backoff + jitter and explicitly say “Do not immediately retry in a tight loop.”
- Mention idempotency: customers should ensure their requests are safe to retry, or use request IDs where applicable.

C) Add one sentence to make it clear:
- “Retry-After is a best-effort hint and may be omitted in some failure modes.”

D) Dedicated/enterprise:
- I’d avoid “enterprise traffic is prioritized” in the Hosted docs. Suggest:
  - “Some accounts may have different limits based on plan and contract.”

If you want, I can push the edits into the markdown and reattach.

—
Wei Chen
Developer Docs
Redwood Inference



From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 29, 2025 at 1:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval

+1 to Wei’s edits.

A couple specific nits for SDK compatibility / consistency:

1) Error payload shape
Right now the draft shows:

{
  "error": {
    "type": "throttled",
    "code": "over_capacity",
    "message": "...",
    "request_id": "..."
  }
}

That’s fine, but we should keep “code” as the stable machine key and use message for human text. Also ensure we don’t introduce a new top-level “reason” field.

2) Header usage
Please avoid “X-RateLimit-*” headers for capacity-protection events. Those headers imply an account-level rate limit and will confuse people when it’s actually fleet pressure. The doc can say:
- For rate limits: include standard rate limit headers
- For capacity events: include Retry-After (when available) + request id

3) Copy edit
Replace:
“Redwood reserves capacity for enterprise customers”
with
“Limits may vary by plan and contract.”

4) One more sentence I’d add:
If you get frequent 429s, contact support with request_id samples and timestamps.

If Wei updates the markdown I can do a final quick pass.

—
Elliot Price
Docs Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 9:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval

Agree with the proposed changes.

Only addition from Enterprise/Dedicated side: in the Hosted docs, please don’t mention “priority lanes” or “enterprise lane.” If we need to explain variance, keep it at plan/contract limits.

For Dedicated docs (separate page), we can be more explicit about reserved capacity and expected behavior.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Product — Dedicated & Enterprise
Redwood Inference



From: Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 12:22 PM PT
Subject: Re: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval
Attachments: hosted-api-throttling-messaging-draft-v4.md

I incorporated edits and attached v4.

Notable changes:
- Renamed section to “HTTP 429 (Throttled)”
- Split causes into:
  - code=rate_limit_exceeded
  - code=over_capacity
- Removed “enterprise prioritized” language, replaced with “limits may vary by plan/contract”
- Added explicit “avoid tight-loop retries” + exponential backoff + jitter
- Added a short “Contact support” paragraph with request_id + timestamps

I left a placeholder line for which rate-limit headers we want to document. Elliot, can you confirm the exact header names you want shown (or if we just keep it generic)?

—
Wei



From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 3:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval

Reviewed v4 — looks good.

On headers: I’d keep the docs generic for now (avoid locking us into exact naming while gateway/router standardization is still rolling out). Suggest:

For rate_limit_exceeded:
- “Rate limit headers may be included to indicate remaining requests and reset time.”

For over_capacity:
- “Retry-After may be included as a best-effort hint.”

Also minor copy tweak:
- In the backoff snippet, add “cap max delay (e.g., 30s)” to prevent unbounded waits.

Otherwise: approved from Docs.

—
Elliot



From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 31, 2025 at 4:38 PM PT
Subject: Re: Throttling & over-capacity messaging (Hosted API docs) — review/approval

Thanks all — aligned.

Wei: please apply Elliot’s last copy tweak (cap max delay) + keep headers generic as suggested, then ship.

Dev: after docs merge, can you sync the Support macro in INT-9032 to match:
- 429 = “Throttled”
- code distinguishes rate_limit_exceeded vs over_capacity
- Ask for request_id + timestamps

Lauren: we’ll handle Dedicated language on the separate page (no references to lanes in Hosted docs).

Marking this approved for merge once v4.1 is up.

—
Nikhil
